title: code-review-pr-scratchpad-maya-thompson-2
content:
PR: reduce-kv-cache-lock-contention (serving-runtime PR #8142)
Author: @mthompson (me) — WIP, pushing suggestions from pairing session
Reviewer notes / quick summary:
- Goal: reduce KV cache lock contention seen under multi-tenant bursts; introduce shard-level locks + optimistic reads. Also tweaks to batching heuristics when cache hits > 0.
- Perf win seen in local sim: tail latency p99 drops ~18% for synthetic mix; need cluster run.
- Risk areas: concurrency invariants for cache eviction + refcount handling; memory regrowth on missed refcounts.

Checklist (my quick review order):
- [x] build + unit tests pass locally
- [x] added new unit tests for shard locking and refcount increments
- [ ] add interleaved stress test in ci (flaky area) -- TODO: add to integration job
- [ ] e2e perf run on staging (simulate bursty multi-tenant traffic)
- [ ] update changelog + release notes (short blurb)

Files to inspect / notes by file:
- kv_cache.rs:
  - line ~320: optimistic read path looks ok but missing fast-path for single-shard hot keys (micro-opt). add a comment explaining tradeoff.
  - eviction logic: potential double-free when refcount reaches 0 concurrently — need atomic decrement ordering (use fetch_sub with release?). TODO: add test simulating concurrent dec/inc and eviction.
- batching_scheduler.py:
  - changed heuristics: if cache_hit_ratio > 0.6 reduce batch timeout by 25% -> rationale: more cached prefixes means shorter new-token work. But for small requests this could increase number of small batches. Add metric to monitor average batch size by tenant.
  - question: should this be configurable per-tenant? For Dedicated customers maybe we want conservative behavior. Flag in config?
- tests/kv_cache_test.rs:
  - good coverage for basic ops, but missing stress/test for eviction race. Add fuzz harness or crossbeam stress scenario.

Refactor ideas (future follow-ups):
- Split KV cache into hot-path C API for extremely hot keys (avoid Rust lock overhead) — big lift, maybe post-1.2.
- Introduce per-tenant token-bucket based batching policy so tenants with stable traffic keep larger batches while bursty tenants decay faster.
- Centralize atomic refcount utilities across runtime (we have two slightly different impls now). Consolidate to a small crate for safety.

Follow-ups / TODOs (short and actionable):
- [ ] Add CI stress job: create `ci/stress/kv-cache-concurrency` job. Start with 10 threads x 100k ops. (Assigned to me)
- [ ] Add metric: `batcher.avg_batch_size_by_tenant` + `cache.hit_ratio_by_tenant` (product asked for tenant-level visibility). Open infra ticket.
- [ ] Run staging perf: @Ethan to run staging scenario with 500 tenants, 100 tps total (mix 30% cacheable). Collect p50/p95/p99 and token cost.
- [ ] Add a short entry in release-notes.md summarizing approach and risk (ops-runbook pointers).

Open questions / uncertain tradeoffs:
- eviction timing: current implementation evicts immediately when refcount==0. Should we add a grace window to avoid churn under rapid in/out? Pro: reduces churn; Con: memory may grow. Suggest telemetry + short TTL (e.g., 30s) configurable.
- shards count: default is 32. Cost/benefit of increasing to 128 for high-concurrency clusters? Likely better p99 but memory overhead. Need empirical evaluation.
- batching heuristic: mixing cache-hit aware behavior with latency SLOs — if we try to shrink batch timeout we may violate e2e latency SLO for interactive tenants. Better approach: per-route SLO hints.

Notes-to-self / quick snippets:
- Add comment in kv_cache.rs: "// NOTE: using seq_cst for now because eviction/race conditions are subtle; consider relaxing once covered by stress tests"
- When adding CI job, reuse the `ci/fixtures/multi-tenant-load` harness.
- Post-merge: run `perf/compare` script against last prod snapshot and tag results in PR.

Draft PR description (top-of-PR to iterate):
---
Reduce KV cache contention by sharding locks and adding optimistic read path. Improves tail latency under bursty multi-tenant traffic. Adds unit tests and preliminary benchmarks.

Known risks: eviction race (mitigated by atomic refcount + test coverage). Requires a staged canary.

Runbook: if memory regrowth observed after deploy, flip `kv_cache.eviction_grace_seconds` to 30 and monitor `cache.entry_count` and OOM events.
---

Quick decisions I'm ok making in this PR (to unblock deploy):
- Keep default shards=32 for now; follow-up PR to experiment with 64/128 in perf run.
- Add short TTL grace of 5s to eviction (configurable flag) vs immediate eviction. Longer TTLs later if needed.

Last-minute TODO (today):
- push unit test that simulates 8 threads contending on same key with random inc/dec and validate no double-free (deadline EOD local).

Links / references:
- related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/5890 (older attempt)
- slack threads: #eng-serving-runtime (see thread pinned: "kv-cache-batching-ideas")
- perf notes: confluence/kv-cache-batching-draft (internal)

If reviewer, look for:
- concurrency invariants: focus on eviction/refcount ordering
- perf regressions: batch size distribution change (watch small-batch increase)
- config knobs: make defaults conservative for Dedicated customers

End of scratchpad.

-- maya
